title: Chapter 24: I Caught the Killer!
html:
The messages had been sent at midnight on consecutive nights. That matched Wang Qi’s story—and made the situation even harder to explain.

How could messages keep coming from the phone of someone who had been dead for years?

Was it supernatural? If so, why had nothing happened to the tenants who had just disturbed the hidden remains?

Something doesn’t fit.Chen Ge mentally lined up the clues, and a new possibility took shape.What if the person sending Wang Qi those messages is also the person responsible for what happened to his fiancée—and for the old fire?

And I think I know who that person is,Chen Ge thought, standing in the cramped wooden cabin.Everyone at Ping An Apartments treats Wang Qi like an outsider and drives him away whenever he appears. Yet he keeps returning to the area. If he isn’t a tenant, he must be staying somewhere nearby.

The landlord insisted there was nowhere else to stay for a long distance around the building. No nearby hotel, no second apartment block. That makes this cabin the obvious place for Wang Qi to be living.

If this is his cabin, then everything changes. The man who spends every day searching for his missing fiancée may be the one responsible for her disappearance.

Chen Ge found it difficult to accept. He had spoken sympathetically with Wang Qi only hours earlier. Now, for the first time, the full danger of the situation sank in.Why keep her clothes? Why send messages to himself from her phone every night? Whether it came from guilt, obsession, or something stranger, Wang Qi’s behavior was deeply unsettling.

Growing more uneasy by the second, Chen Ge checked the phone for anything else that might clarify what had happened.This phone could be important evidence. I need to make sure the police get it.

As he studied the screen, a faint figure appeared in its reflection: a young woman in an old school uniform.

Chen Ge blinked and tried to focus. A sudden chill brushed the back of his neck, and he spun around.

The cabin seemed to freeze around him. Wang Qi was standing only a short distance away, blocking the doorway, his expression completely different from before.

For a moment, neither man moved.

“So close…” Wang Qi’s voice no longer carried its earlier exhaustion. Something feverish had replaced it. Chen Ge said nothing. Whatever had made him turn around, he was grateful for the warning.

“What a waste.” Wang Qi stepped forward. “Relax. You looked through the phone, didn’t you?”

Chen Ge had no idea what he intended, so he kept his distance.

“If you think about it, I never really lied to you.” The lethargy Chen Ge had seen that afternoon was gone; Wang Qi now seemed almost exhilarated. “When we first met, I told you my fiancée was hidden inside the apartments. Remember? I told you the truth.”

He looked down at the clothes scattered near the bed. “I was the one who hid her there.”

His expression twisted as old resentment resurfaced. “I didn’t do anything wrong. She was the one who wanted to leave me. I only wanted her to stay.”

Wang Qi remained between Chen Ge and the door. His voice dropped to a mutter. “I didn’t want any of this. You understand, don’t you? I didn’t mean for it to happen…”

Whatever justification Wang Qi offered, Chen Ge had heard enough. He slipped the woman’s phone into his pocket and kept his attention fixed on the doorway, looking for a chance to escape.

“Everyone hates me,” Wang Qi continued. “They don’t have to say it. I can tell.” His words came faster and less coherently, as though he were trapped inside his own argument and could no longer find the way out.

While Wang Qi talked, Chen Ge slowly adjusted his position, trying to put himself closer to the only exit without drawing attention.

Wang Qi’s voice rose as his agitation increased.

The longer Chen Ge remained trapped in the cabin, the more dangerous the situation became. When Wang Qi’s attention wavered for an instant, Chen Ge lunged for the opening.

It was one of the most reckless decisions Chen Ge had ever made, but hesitation would only leave him trapped.

The sudden move caught Wang Qi off guard.

There was a brief struggle in the darkness.

Chen Ge managed to shove past him and burst through the doorway.

He ran straight into the forest. This time he paid attention to the slope beneath his feet and the spacing of the trees, searching for a route back toward the road. A moving light behind him told him Wang Qi had followed.

Chen Ge did not stop until the trees thinned and the ground leveled beneath him. Only when he reached the road did the sounds behind him fade.

“They should be gone by now.” He had made it several hundred meters along the road when a siren sounded in the distance. Headlights soon appeared around the bend.

Relief nearly knocked the strength out of him. He waved toward the approaching vehicles. “Over here! I’m the one who reported Ping An Apartments!”
